meta.description: Tomorrow, Now. The future will not wait for us — it is built by the bold questions and ideas of young people today. An independently organized TEDx event in Abu Dhabi, UAE.

hero.tagline: Tomorrow is shaped by what we do today.
hero.intro: Nearly half of the UAE's population is under the age of 35. In a nation that believes its greatest asset is its people, creating spaces where ideas are shared across generations has never been more important. TEDxAlFalah Youth is one of those spaces.

about.heading: About the Event
about.body: TEDxAlFalah Youth is an independently organized TED event, designed especially for young men and women in the United Arab Emirates. This event aims to inspire young minds by providing them with a platform to share their ideas, stories, and passions. We believe that the voice of youth is the voice of the future, and that great ideas start with small steps. This event serves youth of all ages and backgrounds, fostering creativity, critical thinking, and collaboration.

theme.title: Tomorrow, Now.
theme.body: The future will not wait for us. It is already here — taking shape in the questions we ask, the ideas we explore, the risks we take, and the bold choices young people make every day. “Tomorrow, Now.” is not about predicting what comes next. It is about claiming it — showing that building tomorrow begins with the thoughts, conversations, and actions of today. Throughout this event, we will explore what it means to be young in a rapidly changing world — and how young people can be the architects of what is coming next. The event brings together speakers and performers who don't just dream about the future, but actively shape it through their work, creativity, and courage. TEDxYouth honors the curiosity, resilience, and vision of young people, while TEDxAlFalah Youth takes this a step further: youth as co-creators of the future — inventing, performing, creating, competing, and asking the bold questions that define a generation. Throughout the day, we will explore the pillars of “Tomorrow, Now.”: the right to question, the right to create, the right to contribute, and the right to act. Together, these four pillars form a roadmap for young people to move from being part of the conversation to shaping it. At the core of this idea is a simple truth: the future belongs to those who build it. And who better to build it than the young minds already shaping our present? So let's start today. Tomorrow, now.

item1.question: Who is eligible to apply as a young speaker?
item1.answer: The young speaker track is open to anyone aged 10 to 18, regardless of nationality or background. We're looking for young people with an original idea, an inspiring personal story, or a unique vision worth sharing on the TEDx stage. No prior public speaking experience is required—just passion and a willingness to grow.

item2.question: Who is eligible to apply as an expert?
item2.answer: The expert track is for adults (18+) who work in fields related to children and youth, such as education, mental health, technology, social innovation, and the arts. We welcome experts with a powerful story or groundbreaking research that can inspire the next generation.

item3.question: What language should the talk be in?
item3.answer: Talks can be delivered in either Arabic or English. If the talk is in a language not understood by the entire audience, we may provide on-screen subtitles to ensure the idea reaches everyone. What matters most is the clarity of the message and its ability to inspire.

item4.question: Will I receive coaching support?
item4.answer: Yes, all selected speakers receive a tailored coaching program that includes multiple one-on-one and group sessions with professional speaking coaches and content developers. We'll help you transform your idea into a compelling TEDx talk, from structure to body language and stage rehearsal.

item5.question: What is the time commitment if I am selected?
item5.answer: Selected speakers should expect to dedicate about 4–6 hours per week over 6–8 weeks before the event. This includes coaching sessions, content writing, and rehearsals. The week before the event, hours increase slightly for final on-stage rehearsals. On event day, you'll need to be present from morning until the event concludes in the evening.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Answers to the most common questions from attendees. Looking for application‑related questions instead?

item1.question: How do I get to the venue?
item1.answer: You can reach the venue easily by public transport or private car. Free parking is available near the main entrance. For detailed directions, maps, and parking guidance, please visit the Venue page.

item2.question: Are parents and guardians allowed to attend?
item2.answer: Yes, parents and guardians are welcome. Everyone (including parents) needs a separate ticket for entry. Tickets can be purchased from the Tickets page.

item3.question: Is there an age requirement to attend as a guest?
item3.answer: The event is open to all ages, but we recommend it for ages 10 and above due to the nature of the talks. Some talks may be more suitable for youth and adults, and there is no upper age limit.

item4.question: Will food and beverages be provided?
item4.answer: Light snacks and drinks will be available for purchase in the lobby. You are also welcome to bring your own snacks. We suggest having a main meal before arriving so you can focus on the talks.

item5.question: What happens if I arrive late?
item5.answer: We recommend arriving before the event starts to enjoy the full experience. If you arrive late, you may be asked to wait and enter only between talks, at the discretion of the organizing team, to avoid disturbing speakers and the audience.

item6.question: Is the event accessible for people with disabilities?
item6.answer: We strive to provide an inclusive environment for all. Wheelchair‑accessible entrances, designated seating near the stage, and other support services are available. For more details, please visit the Venue page or contact us.

item7.question: Will the talks be recorded or live‑streamed?
item7.answer: The talks will be recorded and later shared on the official TEDx YouTube channel. A live stream may also be available – follow our social media channels for updates.

item8.question: How can I volunteer or get involved?
item8.answer: We always welcome passionate individuals! You can volunteer by reaching out via the contact form on our website, mentioning 'Volunteer' in the subject line. We'll send you the details and requirements.

item9.question: I have another question – who can I contact?
item9.answer: Get in touch through the contact form on our homepage, or email us directly at marhaba@tedxalfalahyouth.com. We'll be happy to help.
